summary: Today’s pulse tracks Trump ousts Kimberly Guilfoyle as US ambassador to Greece after corruption allegations, Pope Leo admitted to hospital for operation to remove growth on lung, and Kimberly Guilfoyle denies allegations of misconduct as she resigns as US ambassador to Greece – live. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are tupac, years, and guilfoyle. In the background, Duane Keith Davis sentenced to 40 years over 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur and Saudi coalition strikes fuel depot near Yemen's capital keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Trump ousts Kimberly Guilfoyle as US ambassador to Greece after corruption allegations
headlines.description: Guilfoyle the allegations of improper conduct are "false" and being ambassador was the "honour of a lifetime".

headlines.title: Pope Leo admitted to hospital for operation to remove growth on lung
headlines.description: Vatican says surgery that will determine whether the nodule is malignant will take place on Tuesday afternoon Pope Leo underwent an operation on Tuesday to remove a small growth from his lung, which the Vatican said concluded “successfully, on schedule and as planned”. In a rare moment of Vatican transparency, Leo, 71, said during his angelus prayer on Sunday that doctors had found a small nodule on his lung during a check-up , adding that it was “well-contained” and detected early.

headlines.title: Duane Keith Davis sentenced to 40 years over 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur
headlines.description: ‘You don’t get to take a man from his family … and just walk away from it,’ judge says as former gang leader sentenced Tupac trial spotlights decades of US police failures in solving the case Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former California gang leader convicted of murder for orchestrating the 1996 fatal shooting of rapper Tupac Shakur , has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison. “For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing … ‘Yeah, I was involved in this. But I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,’” Judge Carli Kierny said Tuesday as she delivered the sentence.

headlinePool.title: Judge orders Trump administration to halt work on historic DC golf course
headlinePool.description: District judge Ana Reyes halts tree-cutting at the East Potomac golf course until 26 October, and now requires advance notice before making course changes US district judge Ana Reyes on Tuesday ordered a halt to tree-cutting at the East Potomac golf course until 26 October, putting a further pause on work at the historic Washington DC course that has been part of Donald Trump’s plans to remake the country'’s capital city. Reyes issued the order one day after a tense three-hour hearing in which she harshly criticized the government for having deceived her with its actions over the holiday weekend.

headlinePool.title: ‘There was a chance to stop him’: Parents react with fury to paedophile nursery worker revelations
headlinePool.description: More than 50 families call for investigation into how Vincent Chan was allowed to return to job after inquiry by nursery The parents of the victims of paedophile nursery worker Vincent Chan have reacted with fury to the news that he was cleared to return to work after “significant concerns” were raised by the parent of a young girl. As first revealed in the Guardian , Chan was reported to his employer, the nursery chain Bright Horizons, by a concerned parent in 2021. After being investigated by Bright Horizons, with the knowledge of Camden council, Chan was cleared to return to work at the nursery on the Finchley Road in north-west London. A year later, in 2022, Chan filmed himself abusing three-year-old girls in his care.

headlinePool.title: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations
headlinePool.description: The school has faced an uproar over how it handled assault allegations brought by a woman known as Jane Doe.

headlinePool.title: California coastal homes battered and bruised after weekend of intense waves and flooding
headlinePool.description: Boardwalk destroyed in Long Beach and homes damaged, while Baja California in Mexico and Las Vegas also affected Southern California coastal communities are picking up the pieces after a weekend of extreme weather brought flooding that overtook city streets and intense waves battered beachside homes. The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel hit Mexico’s Baja California over the weekend as well as southern California and Las Vegas. While meteorologists noted that Rachel weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it approached California, it still left a trail of destruction.

headlinePool.title: Pope's surgery to remove lump on lung 'concluded successfully', Vatican says
headlinePool.description: Pope Leo has said the growth is "contained" and had been found "at a very early stage".

headlinePool.title: 'If we don't scream, they won't listen to us': Student protesters speak to BBC in Paris
headlinePool.description: Student protesters in France have told the BBC's James Waterhouse that they will continue to take action until change has been made. The protests have now entered their fourth week.

headlinePool.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle steps down as US ambassador to Greece after alleged misconduct
headlinePool.description: White House asked Guilfoyle, who is alleged to have sought a bill payment from a Trump donor, to resign from post US politics live – latest updates Kimberly Guilfoyle is stepping down as US ambassador to Greece after weeks of reports that she sought payment from a Trump donor in exchange for access to administration officials. The decision, announced by the White House on Tuesday morning, ends the diplomatic career of one of Donald Trump’s longest-standing political allies. It came after the US president and Marco Rubio, the secretary of state, were reported to have grown furious over the allegations.

headlinePool.title: Far-right and Iran add to mix of terror threats UK faces – not to mention AI
headlinePool.description: Annual update from MI5 chief highlighted a complex cocktail that could have real-life consequences for Britain MI5’s annual threat update covers so much ground it is easy to feel anxious. The terror threat has become more diverse, with far-right anti-migrant threats on the rise; while Iran has now firmly emerged alongside Russia as a country seeking to undertake violent and deadly plots in the UK. “There is no law of physics dictating that rising state threats will be accompanied by diminishing terrorist threats,” MI5’s director general, Ken McCallum, said , although one of his core messages was that people and the country at large needed to focus on being more resilient. “In this new world, we should expect to be tested.”
